attempts.summary: Implemented daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed). Ansible-core 2.20 on node2 requires Python >=3.9 for standard modules, but node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) only has Python 2.7/3.5, so the playbook uses the raw module (pure SSH, no target-side Python module dependency) to deploy /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily rotation, rotate 7, compress, and copytruncate, then validates it with logrotate -d. Functional test with logrotate -f confirmed the log file kept its inode (copytruncate) and the application could keep writing to the same path immediately after rotation, with prior content preserved in app.log.1.gz. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured baseline boot_id/service state, rebooted each node one at a time via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified the logrotate config, rotated archive, and continued-write behavior on node1, plus a successful idempotent re-run of the playbook from node2 post-restart.
